answer: Every agent identity must first burn a single ember of admission: a one-time proof-of-work that cannot be reused or split. The network then arranges all active identities on a terrace of graded trust levels, where each level requires progressively more attested history to climb. Clones planted by one attacker form a dense grove, all sharing the same generation footprint, which community detection on the trust graph exposes immediately. Since burning an ember costs real compute and a grove needs many embers at once, the attacker's cost per fake identity is steep and non-reducible.
